prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: what happened to the beautiful new planes going to DTW. No plugs, entertainment system. You had us at hello now gone?!?!
Delta: Hi. I am so sorry. What flight were you on? I can look to see what the other planes have for the same routing. Thanks.  *TMS

Customer: thanks for the great service and flights Home.  New planes are awesome! #tv #entertainment #chargingstation #coachstyleislokefirstclass
Delta: Good evening, Jessica. You're very welcome!  *ABN

Customer: Here we go  ready to make new memories! https://t.co/wdb6WsxK4C
Delta: Thanks for flying with us,Anne. Happy travels!  *AJZ

Customer: $35 difference to change a flight for a new itinerary. Fabulous! 
So you new change total is $235. I will never fly  again. Ever.
Delta: *Elise? *AAB

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: praise):
"""New #planes, new uniforms - a lot of new things at   #avgeek #DeltaFlyAway

https://t.co/ssdf5ed2R9"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Thanks for sharing your excitement! We’re thrilled you love the new planes and uniforms.
